title: Language Techniques (KS4 English Language)
subject: English Language
strapline: The devices writers use to create effects — and how to name them.
facts: A simile compares using "like" or "as": "as brave as a lion".
A metaphor says one thing IS another: "the classroom was a zoo".
Personification gives human qualities to non-human things: "the wind whispered".
Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds: "slippery, slimy snakes".
Onomatopoeia is a word that sounds like its meaning: "buzz", "crash".
The "rule of three" lists three things for emphasis; hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration.
Analyse the EFFECT, not just the label — say what the device makes the reader think or feel.

quick_quiz.q: Name the device in "the stars danced in the sky".
What is a comparison using "like" or "as" called?

teacher_tips: Always push from "spot the device" to "explain the effect on the reader".
Model with a single quotation analysed several ways.
Keep simile vs metaphor distinct — the most-confused pair.
